title.narrative: Northern Rural Infrastructure Development Sector Project

description.narrative:
The Project will address sector constraints by rehabilitating existing irrigation facilities and, where appropriate, developing new ones, as well as rehabilitating and upgrading rural access roads from district centers and village cluster centers to villages. To enhance the impact of subproject investments, the project will support (i) technical extension services to subproject beneficiaries, (ii) producer groups to coordinate supplies of agricultural produce to markets and/or processors, (iii) contracted agricultural production with price incentives based on quality, and (iv) initiatives to secure tenure and access to land for sedentary agricultural production and land rezoning to protect the integrity of watersheds and reservoirs
above rehabilitated irrigation systems. This will contribute to improving agricultural productivity, diversifying crops, and commercializing the low-performing agriculture sector in the northern region. These investments will be complemented by (i) institutional capacity building for national, provincial, and district agencies towards a sector development approach and (ii) heightened awareness of gender issues and the participation of local communities in designing and efficiently implementing about 25 subprojects. The project will be implemented in the four northern provinces of Bokeo, Luang Namtha, Oudomxay, and Phongsaly, which have a combined population of 760,000 people, a third of whom are considered poor.

description.narrative: Increased agricultural productivity in the four northern provinces of Bokeo, Luang Namtha, Oudomxay, and Phongsaly

Agriculture productivity in rice equivalent increased from 3 tons/hectare in 2010 to 5 tons/hectare by 2024 Progress/Status: As December 2023:
This target has been achieved, the average rice productivity 22 subprojects is 4.8 to 5.5 tons per ha in 2022 wet season and dry seas in 2021/2022. The average crop productivity equivalent with rice is 6 tons per has in dry season. The collected data on rice and crops production and prices per hectare by subprojects starting from October 2020 to March 2023 which will be used to (i) assess the achievement of project outcome, (ii) evaluate the project's impact, and (iii) reevaluate the project economic internal rate of return.
---------------------------------------------------------------- - The project focus on increase in rice production with high uniform quality seeds and strengthening of farmer's skill and knowledge about rice seed multiplication.
- The project applied system of rice intensification (SRI) technique for rice seed multiplication demonstration (RSMD).
Phase I subprojects: - 2018-19 wet season, the average rice yield in Nam Beng was 4.0 ton/ha with a total cropped area of 314 ha and 3.5 ton/ha with a total cropped area of 420 ha.
- 2019-20 dry season, the average rice yield was 5 ton/ha with the cropped area of 205.7 ha.
- in 2021 wet season, the average rice yield at Nam Beng and Nam Oun was 5.3 ton/ha with a total cropped area of 386 ha and 420 ha, respectively.
- In 2022 wet season, the average rice yield in most of the rehabilitated irrigation command area increased to 5.5 tons per ha. Farmers focused on cash crops in dry seasons because of higher price and production. Data Source: Key commercial crop production statistical reports by provincial and district agriculture and forestry offices Actual value:

Batch 1 activities are goats raising, cardamom and vegetable planting. Output: Production and productivity-enhancing rural infrastructure constructed and/or rehabilitated Indicator: 225 kilometers of rural access roads rehabilitated by 2023 Achievement: 154.1 Progress/Status: To date, a total of 154.1 km of rural access/O&M road of 22 PRI subprojects of phase I, II and III was identified, among which, 26.2 km of phase I, 44.2 km of phase II, 21.4 km of phase III and 62.3 km of phase IV.
Total length of rural access road of all the completed 26 subprojects (under original project) is estimated at 167.47 km. Data Source: - National project management office (NPMO) and provincial project office (PPO) quarterly progress and monitoring reports
- NPMO and PPO consolidated subproject completion reports

Output: Capacity of national, provincial, and district agencies strengthened to enable a sector development approach Indicator: Irrigation subsector review completed by 2017 Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Contract with IWMI/WorldFish was signed on 24 May 2018 and mobilization was on 2 July 2018. - An inception workshop was held on 25 September 2018 to discuss the scope of the review. - A midterm workshop was held on 28 June 2019 - The draft final report was submitted to DOI in September 2019. - Regional workshop was held on 18 November 2019 in Luang Prabang, 20 November 2019 in Pakse and 22 November 2019 in Vientiane Capital. - Final report was submitted in March 2020 and submitted to ADB on September 2020. Data Source: NPMO and PPO quarterly progress and monitoring reports

Output: Productivity and impact-enhancing initiatives adopted Indicator: 35 watershed management plans with associated land rezoning implemented; cadastral maps for 48 subprojects irrigation command areas and at least 5,000 water user group members obtain land ownership certificates by June 2023 Achievement: 29 Progress/Status: Watershed management: - Training program (i) how to use GPS; (ii) prepare the irrigation block map; and (iii) O&M were conducted for 2 groups in Luang Namtha and Bokeo; and Oudomxai and Phongsaly provinces. - Total 37 participants, out of which Hmong 1, Lue 6, phounoi 2, Kummu 2, and Lao 13. All participants were male.
Watershed area: Total 1,173 km2 were identified. Cadastral map: - 2 cadastral maps for Nam Beng and Nam Oun PRI subproject were completed during detail design in 2017. - 7 cadastral maps for Phase II subprojects have been completed during detailed design in 2018. - 7 cadastral maps for Phase III subprojects are on-going.
Land ownership certificate: - The consultation with PONRE on land titling activity was conducted from December 2017 to March 2018. - As of December 2019, 3,297 plots of land have been issued the land title certificate. GIS Training: GIS training program II was carried out 10 to 21 June 2019 with a total 40 participants of 4 provinces. Data Source: NPMO and PPO quarterly progress and monitoring reports

Output: Productivity and impact-enhancing initiatives adopted Indicator: 48 water farm producer groups supply contracts ratified by district agriculture and forestry offices by December 2023 to supply private processors for value addition through processing Achievement: 31 Progress/Status: Farmer Producer Groups: All WUG members have two main functions/objectives/responsibilities for i) O&M of Irrigation Facilities, and ii) Irrigated Crop Production. In this context, all WUG members are the FPG members.
Agriculture Extension Activities: The progress of AEA are: 1. 20 training Rice Seed Multiplication Demonstration by SRI technique. 2. 5 training on Production and O&M. 3. 2 contract farming implementation. 4. 40 field cross visit and experience exchange. 5. 3 farmer study tour. Data Source: NPMO and PPO quarterly progress and monitoring reports

Output: Productivity and impact-enhancing initiatives adopted Indicator: 48 water user groups and farm producer groups operating by December 2023, with women comprising 30% of their members Achievement: 83 Progress/Status: To date, a total of 83 WUGs at 22 subprojects of Phase I, II, III and IV was established.
Phase I: 3 WUGs of 2 subprojects have been established with 27 committee members, 11 female (41%)
Phase II: 28 WUGs of 7 subprojects were established with 155 committee members, 56 female (47%)
Phase III: 31 WUGs of 7 subprojects were established with 175 committee members, 64 female (37%)
Phase IV: 18 WUGs of 6 subprojects were established with 108 committee members, 29 female (27%) Data Source: NPMO and PPO quarterly progress and monitoring reports

Output: Production and productivity-enhancing rural infrastructure constructed and/or rehabilitated Indicator: An estimated 12,100 ha of command area served by rehabilitated gravity irrigation structures by 2023 Achievement: 2548 Progress/Status: To date, a total of 8,794 ha of command area of 22 PRI subprojects of Phase I, II, III and IV was identified, among which, 806 ha of phase I, 2,641 ha of phase II, 2,799 ha of phase III and 2,548 ha of phase IV.
Total command area of all the completed 24 irrigation subprojects under G0235-LAO (original project) is estimated at 5,387 ha. Data Source: - National project management office (NPMO) and provincial project office (PPO) quarterly progress and monitoring reports
- NPMO and PPO consolidated subproject completion reports

In general, male will responsible for engineering-related while female are respond for non-engineering field.
